mainTopic: When does evening קריאת שמע begin? The meaning of וּבָא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְטָהֵר, the different time markers (the כהן, the poor man, people's meals), and רבי יוסי's split-second בין השמשות.
overview: The פסוק says a טמא כהן may eat תרומה after "the sun sets and וְטָהֵר." רבה בר רב שילא proves from the wording that וְטָהֵר means the day is 'cleared,' so full sunset is needed. In ארץ ישראל they reached the same answer from a ברייתא that gives צאת הכוכבים as the sign. The גמרא then compares our משנה's start time for evening שמע with other ברייתות. These use a poor man's meal, people's Friday-night meal, and more. A פסוק in נחמיה hints that night begins at צאת הכוכבים. After going back and forth, the גמרא concludes that the poor man's time is different from the כהן's time, and later than it. Finally, רבי מאיר answers רבי יהודה's objection about the כהנים immersing by day: he follows רבי יוסי, for whom בין השמשות lasts only a blink of an eye.

steps.title: Maybe it means only the start of sunset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reading: "ובא השמש" could mean the sun's light starts to fade, and "וטהר" could mean the man becomes pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it means the setting of its light, and "וְטָהֵר" means the man becomes pure?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the assumption that the פסוק means full nightfall. It offers a different way to read the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "ובא השמש" only means the start of sunset, then the כהן could eat תרומה earlier, while it is still somewhat light. In that reading "וטהר" describes the person becoming טהור, not the day ending. That would also move the start time of evening קריאת שמע earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / maybe. Opens a different possibility
The setting of its light, meaning the beginning of sunset
"And he/it is pure," the word in the פסוק being analyzed
The man becomes pure

steps.confusionAlert: The whole argument is about who or what is the subject of וְטָהֵר: the person, or the day. Keep that question in mind for every step.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is the setting of its light,
phrases.notes: He means the very start of sunset, when the sun's light begins to go, not full nightfall.

phrases.english: and what is "and it is pure"? The man becomes pure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question of how we know the פסוק means full sunset and a 'cleared' day.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that "ובא השמש וטהר" means full sunset, with the day becoming 'pure.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words could just as easily mean the start of sunset, with וטהר describing the person, so the proof is not forced.

steps.title: Grammar proves 'וטהר' refers to the day
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא answers that if the פסוק meant the man, it would say וְיִטְהָר. The form וְטָהֵר means the day is 'cleared,' as in common speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: If so, let the פסוק say "וְיִטְהָר" (he will become pure). What does "וְטָהֵר" mean? The day is cleared, as people say: "The sun has set and the day is cleared."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא rejects the challenge by looking closely at the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a person becoming pure, the expected form is וְיִטְהָר (future tense). The Torah instead wrote וְטָהֵר, which matches an everyday saying about the day being 'cleared' at nightfall. So the פסוק means full sunset, when no daylight is left.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Introduces a problem with the suggested reading
Let the פסוק say. Argues the Torah would have used different wording
"And he will become pure," the future form that would describe a person
The day is cleared, meaning no daylight remains
As people say. Proof from everyday language

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the time a טמא כהן may eat תרומה at full nightfall. That is the anchor for the earliest time of evening קריאת שמע in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
If so, let the verse say: "and he will become pure,"
so what is "and it is pure"? The day is cleared,
as people say:
"The sun has set and the day has cleared."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 with a proof from grammar.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linguistic proof from the verb form plus common speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: וטהר could describe the man becoming pure at the start of sunset.
steps.terutzMaskana: וטהר describes the day being cleared, so full sunset is required.
steps.whatToRemember: וְטָהֵר = the day is cleared, not the man. So a טמא כהן eats תרומה only after full sunset.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they raised it as a question
steps.stepSummary: The sages of ארץ ישראל had not heard רבה בר רב שילא's proof, so they raised both readings as a question. The next step answers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In מערבא they had not heard this teaching of רבה בר רב שילא, and they asked: Does "ובא השמש" mean the full setting of the sun, and "וטהר" means the day is cleared? Or perhaps it means the setting of its light, and "וטהר" means the man becomes pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that in ארץ ישראל the same question came up as an unanswered dilemma. This sets up the next step, where they find an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the grammar proof, both readings seemed possible to them, so they listed both options side by side. This shows the פסוק alone did not settle the issue for them, and they needed another source.

keyTerms.meaning: "The West," meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)
They had not heard it
They raised it as a question (a בעיא)
The full setting of the sun

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַעֲרָבָא, הָא דְּרַבָּהּ בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא
phrases.english: In the West, this teaching of Rabba bar Rav Sheila
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: they had not heard,
and they raised it as a question:
Is this "and the sun sets" the full setting of its sun,
and what is "and it is pure"? The day is cleared,
or perhaps it is the setting of its light,
and what is "and it is pure"? The man becomes pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as step 1, but in ארץ ישראל, where step 2's answer was unknown.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ובא השמש means full sunset (day cleared) or the start of sunset (man purified).

steps.title: Resolved from the ברייתא: stars coming out
steps.stepSummary: They resolved the question from a ברייתא that gives צאת הכוכבים as the sign for when כהנים eat תרומה. That proves full sunset and a 'cleared' day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then they resolved it from a ברייתא. Since the ברייתא teaches "a sign for the matter is צאת הכוכבים," learn from it: it is the full setting of the sun, and "וטהר" means the day is cleared.
steps.whatsHappening: The sages of ארץ ישראל answer their own question using a ברייתא, and they reach the same conclusion as רבה בר רב שילא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the time כהנים eat תרומה is marked by the stars coming out. Stars only appear after full sunset, not at its start. So "ובא השמש" must mean full sunset, and וטהר must refer to the day.

keyTerms.meaning: They resolved it (answered the בעיא)
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
A sign for the matter, a practical marker
The coming out of the stars, nightfall
Learn from it, a conclusion drawn from a source

steps.whatToRemember: Two paths, one answer: בבל proved it from grammar (וְטָהֵר, not וְיִטְהָר), and ארץ ישראל proved it from the ברייתא (צאת הכוכבים). Both say full sunset, and the day is cleared.

phrases.english: And then they resolved it from a baraita.
Since it teaches in the baraita,
"A sign for the matter is the coming out of the stars."
Learn from it: it is the full setting of its sun,
and what is "and it is pure"? The day is cleared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ובא השמש means full sunset, and וטהר means the day is cleared, proven by the sign of צאת הכוכבים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: סימן לדבר צאת הכוכבים

steps.title: The poor person's meal versus the כהנים eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's start time and sets it against a ברייתא that uses a poor person's meal as the time for evening שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: evening שמע starts when the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה. But a ברייתא says: evening שמע starts when a poor man sits down to eat bread with salt, and ends when he gets up from his meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to give a different time for evening שמע than the משנה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures the time by the כהנים, while the ברייתא measures it by a poor person's simple meal. The ברייתא also gives an end time: when he finishes eating. That is much earlier than the end time the משנה gives, so the two sources look like they clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted it.' This brings a source that seems to contradict the one just quoted.
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן. He may only eat it once he is pure.
A poor person
His bread with salt, a poor man's simple meal

phrases.english: The Master said: From the time that the priests
phrases.notes: Here 'the Master' means our משנה. The גמרא is quoting its words again.

phrases.english: enter to eat their teruma.
And they contrasted it [with this]:
From when does one recite Shema in the evening?
From when the poor person enters
to eat his bread with salt,
until the time that he gets up
to leave his meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's start time and opens a new contradiction from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's start time for evening שמע: when the כהנים eat תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives a different marker (a poor man's meal) and a much earlier end time. So it seems to argue with the משנה.

steps.title: Does the start time also argue with the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the end time in the ברייתא surely argues with the משנה. It asks whether the start time does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second half of the ברייתא (the end time) certainly argues with our משנה. But the first half (the start time): shall we say it also argues with our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא splits the ברייתא into two halves and asks about the first half only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor man finishes his meal long before the end of the first watch, so the end time clearly disagrees with the משנה. The open question is only the start: is a poor man sitting down to eat a different moment than the כהנים going in to eat?

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause, the second part of a teaching
The first clause, the opening part of a teaching
Disagrees, argues
Our משנה

phrases.english: The latter clause certainly disagrees with our mishna.
phrases.notes: The 'latter clause' is the end time, when the poor man gets up from his meal.

phrases.english: The first clause, shall we say
that it disagrees with our mishna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the contradiction from step 5 down to the start time only.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the poor man's start time a different moment from the כהנים' start time in the משנה?

steps.title: The poor man and the כהן eat at the same time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the poor man's meal and the כהן's eating of תרומה happen at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The poor man and the כהן are one and the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the start time does not argue with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are two different pictures of the same moment. When the poor man sits down to eat is exactly when the כהן may eat תרומה. So only the end time is a real disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: One measure, the same amount of time

phrases.english: No, the poor person and the priest
are one and the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עָנִי וְכֹהֵן חַד שִׁיעוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The poor man's meal and the כהן's eating of תרומה are the same moment, so the start times agree.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: when people eat on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, where רבי מאיר says evening שמע starts when people sit down to eat on Friday night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another source was contrasted: From when do we begin to read שמע in the evening? From when people go in to eat their bread on Friday nights. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to compare with what it just said. This sets up a new difficulty that the גמרא will work through next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's sign is a third marker: people eating on ערב שבת. The גמרא just said the poor man and the כהן share one time. Now it must check how רבי מאיר's time fits with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Evening
Friday evenings, the start of שבת

phrases.english: And they contrasted it: From when does one begin
to recite Shema in the evening?
From the time that people enter
to eat their bread on Shabbat eves,
the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: מֵאֵימָתַי מַתְחִילִין לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּעַרְבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source right after the answer in step 7 that the poor man and the כהן share one time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The start time for evening שמע as set out in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר uses yet another marker. The גמרא will need to show how it fits with the times already discussed.

steps.title: The חכמים: when the כהנים may eat, marked by the stars
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים in the ברייתא say evening שמע begins when the כהנים are allowed to eat תרומה, and the sign is when the stars come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: from the time the כהנים are allowed to eat their תרומה. The sign for this is when the stars come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the view of the חכמים. It matches our משנה and adds a clear sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say the same thing as our משנה, using the כהנים and their תרומה. They add a visible sign, צאת הכוכבים, so anyone can tell when that time has come.

keyTerms.meaning: Entitled, allowed
A sign for the matter, a way to recognize it
When the stars come out, nightfall

phrases.english: And the Sages say: From the time that the priests
are entitled to eat their teruma.
A sign for the matter: the emergence of the stars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other opinion in the same ברייתא, opposite רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Evening שמע begins when the כהנים may eat תרומה, which is marked by צאת הכוכבים.

steps.title: A hint from נחמיה that night starts with the stars
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings two פסוקים from נחמיה as a hint, not a full proof, that the day ends when the stars come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no real proof for this, there is a hint. It says: 'We did the work, and half of them held spears from dawn until the stars came out.' And it says: 'The night was a guard for us, and the day was for work.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא supports the חכמים' sign of צאת הכוכבים with a hint from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says the work went on from dawn until the stars came out. The second פסוק calls the work time 'day' and the guarding time 'night.' Put together, the 'day' ran until צאת הכוכבים, so night begins then.

keyTerms.meaning: A real proof
A hint or allusion to the matter, weaker than a proof
Dawn, when the first light rises

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים's time, when the כהנים may eat תרומה, is צאת הכוכבים, the moment night begins.
steps.confusionAlert: The second פסוק is needed. The first alone could mean the workers simply worked late into the night. The second shows that the whole work time was called 'day.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter, as it is said:
"And we were doing the work,
and half of them were holding the spears
from dawn until the stars came out,"
And it says:
"And the night was a guard for us,
and the day was for work."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the sign of צאת הכוכבים given by the חכמים in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the day ends and night begins at צאת הכוכבים

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא add a second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra phrase 'and it says' adds, since the first פסוק already seems to prove the point.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and it says' come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why the ברייתא brought a second פסוק after the first one. This question sets up the next step, which explains the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק from נחמיה already seems to show that the workday lasted until the stars came out. So bringing a second פסוק looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what the second פסוק proves that the first one does not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': a phrase used to bring an additional פסוק as a further source

phrases.english: What is added by 'and it says'?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא in step 10, which used 'and it says' to bring a second פסוק from נחמיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how the two פסוקים in step 10 work together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second פסוק teaches that the first פסוק did not.

steps.title: The second פסוק closes a loophole in the first
steps.stepSummary: Someone could say night starts at sunset and the workers just worked late. The second פסוק shows the time before the stars is called 'day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say that night really starts when the sun sets, and the workers simply stayed late and came early. So come and hear the second פסוק: 'The night will be a guard for us, and the day will be for work.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the first פסוק alone could be read another way. The second פסוק blocks that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first פסוק, someone could argue that night starts at sunset and the workers were just extra devoted, working into the night. The second פסוק calls the work time 'day' and the guarding time 'night.' Since they worked until the stars came out, the time until the stars is clearly called day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say': brings up a possible objection before answering it
The sun sets
They stay late into the dark and start early

steps.whatToRemember: The day ends at צאת הכוכבים, when the stars come out, and not at sunset. The second פסוק calls the whole work time 'day.'

phrases.english: And if you will say that from when the sun sets,
it is already night,
and they were the ones who stayed late and started early,
come and hear:
'And the night shall be a guard for us,'
'and the day for work.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק rules out the idea that the workers simply worked into the night. It shows that the work time, until the stars appear, is called 'day.'

steps.title: If the poor man and the כהן are the same time, the חכמים would match רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes the poor man and ordinary people eat at the same time. It then challenges step 7: that would make the חכמים say the same as רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You would think that the poor man and ordinary people eat at one time. And if you say the poor man and the כהן are one time, then the חכמים are the same as רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the starting times for evening שמע and attacks the earlier answer (step 7) that the poor man and the כהן share one time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said the start is when people sit down to their Friday-night meal. The חכמים said the start is when כהנים eat תרומה. If the poor man equals ordinary people, and the poor man also equals the כהן, then all three are one time. Then the חכמים and רבי מאיר would not really disagree, which makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind: what you would first assume
One and the same time measure
This is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: There are three different groups here: the poor man (from the first ברייתא), the כהן eating תרומה (the חכמים), and ordinary people at their Friday-night meal (רבי מאיר). Keep them apart in your head.

phrases.english: It enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: דְּעָנִי וּבְנֵי אָדָם חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא.
phrases.english: that the poor man and ordinary people are one time.
phrases.notes: 'Ordinary people' are the ones רבי מאיר spoke about, who sit down to eat on Friday night (step 8).

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ עָנִי וְכֹהֵן חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא,
phrases.english: And if you say that the poor man and the כהן are one time,
then the חכמים are the same as רבי מאיר?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּעָנִי וּבְנֵי אָדָם חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the פסוקים and challenges the answer from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 7 that the poor man and the כהן eat at the same time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If poor man = ordinary people and poor man = כהן, then כהן = ordinary people. That would erase the argument between the חכמים and רבי מאיר.

steps.title: So the poor man and the כהן must be different times
steps.stepSummary: Based on the challenge, the גמרא first concludes that the poor man's time and the כהן's time are separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the poor man has his own time and the כהן has his own time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws what looks like a conclusion from the challenge: the answer of step 7 must be wrong. This is only a first try, and the very next step pushes back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the poor man and the כהן were the same, the חכמים would equal רבי מאיר. To keep a real argument, the גמרא suggests the poor man and the כהן are different times. That would also mean the first ברייתא's start time argues with the משנה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this: draws a conclusion
Separately, on its own

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this
that the poor man is a separate time
and the כהן is a separate time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the challenge in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A first conclusion: the poor man's time and the כהן's time are different. Step 15 overturns this.

steps.title: No: the poor man equals the כהן, but not ordinary people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the conclusion. It keeps the poor man and the כהן as one time and instead says the poor man and ordinary people are different times.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The poor man and the כהן are one time, and the poor man and ordinary people are not one time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 14 and saves the answer of step 7. It does this by dropping the assumption it started with in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 13 depended on the idea that the poor man and ordinary people eat at the same time. The גמרא now denies that. So the poor man still matches the כהן, and the חכמים still really disagree with רבי מאיר, whose 'ordinary people' eat at a different time.

keyTerms.meaning: No: rejects the previous conclusion
Not

steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: poor man = כהן eating תרומה (stars coming out). Ordinary people at their Friday-night meal are a separate time. Only רבי מאיר holds that view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the answer of step 7, that the first ברייתא's start time does not argue with the משנה. It also keeps a real argument between the חכמים and רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, עָנִי וְכֹהֵן חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא,
phrases.english: No, the poor man and the כהן are one time,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָנִי וּבְנֵי אָדָם לָאו חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא.
phrases.english: and the poor man and ordinary people are not one time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עָנִי וְכֹהֵן חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 14 by denying the assumption that opened step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion of step 14 and the starting assumption of step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge wrongly assumed that the poor man and ordinary people eat at the same time.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the poor man's time and the כהן's time separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions step 15's idea that the poor man and the כהן share one time. It quotes a ברייתא with six opinions on when the evening שמע begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the poor man and the כהן really one time? There is a source that seems to say otherwise. From when do we start saying the evening שמע? רבי אליעזר says: from when the day becomes holy on Friday evening. רבי יהושע says: from when the כהנים are pure and can eat their תרומה. רבי מאיר says: from when the כהנים go to the מקוה to be able to eat their תרומה. רבי יהודה asked him: but the כהנים go to the מקוה while it is still day! רבי חנינא says: from when the poor man sits down to eat his bread with salt. רבי אחאי (some say רבי אחא) says: from when most people sit down to their meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 15 by bringing a ברייתא that lists many opinions about when the evening שמע starts. This step is setting up the challenge. The next step will point out exactly where the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the poor man and the כהן eat at the same time. This ברייתא gives a separate opinion for each one: רבי יהושע uses the כהן and רבי חנינא uses the poor man. Since they appear as two separate opinions, the גמרא suspects they are not the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction: one source is set against another
A set time or measure
The day became holy, meaning שבת has begun
They go into a מקוה
While it is still day
To recline at a meal, meaning to sit down to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two כהן opinions. רבי יהושע uses the time the כהנים become pure (at night). רבי מאיר uses the earlier time when they go into the מקוה (still daytime).

phrases.english: And are the poor man and the priest one time?
And they raised a contradiction:
From when do we begin to read שמע in the evening?
From the time the day becomes holy on Friday evenings,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
From the time the priests are purified
to eat their terumah.
Rabbi Meir says,
From the time the priests immerse to eat their terumah.
Rabbi Yehudah said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא כֹּהֲנִים מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם הֵם טוֹבְלִים?
phrases.english: But don't the priests immerse while it is still day?
Rabbi Chanina says

phrases.aramaic: מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁעָנִי נִכְנָס לֶאֱכוֹל פִּתּוֹ בְּמֶלַח.
phrases.english: from the time the poor man goes in to eat his bread with salt.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחַאי וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי אַחָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Achai, and some say Rabbi Acha, says:

phrases.aramaic: מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁרוֹב בְּנֵי אָדָם נִכְנָסִין לְהָסֵב.
phrases.english: From the time most people go in to recline for their meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעָנִי וְכֹהֵן חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15's claim that the poor man and the כהן share one time.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15: the poor man and the כהן eat at the same time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists the כהן's time (רבי יהושע) and the poor man's time (רבי חנינא) as separate opinions.

steps.title: If the times were the same, רבי חנינא would just be repeating רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: if the poor man and the כהן eat at the same time, then רבי חנינא and רבי יהושע are saying the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the poor man and the כהן are one time, then רבי חנינא is the same as רבי יהושע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now says out loud what is wrong with step 15, using the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would not list two opinions that mean exactly the same thing. רבי יהושע's time is when the כהן eats, and רבי חנינא's time is when the poor man eats. If those were the same moment, there would be no reason to list both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say
That is the same as

phrases.english: And if you say
that the poor man and the priest are one time,
then Rabbi Chanina is the same as Rabbi Yehoshua!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ עָנִי וְכֹהֵן חַד שִׁעוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the explicit contradiction from the ברייתא quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15's claim that the poor man and the כהן share one time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two separately listed opinions in the ברייתא would be identical, which makes no sense.

steps.title: The poor man's time and the כהן's time are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the poor man and the כהן have separate times, which brings back the conclusion of step 14.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it clear from here that the poor man's time is one thing and the כהן's time is another? Yes, that is what we learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge stands, so the גמרא concludes that the poor man's time and the כהן's time are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This overturns step 15 and brings back what step 14 had said. Now that we know the two times are different, the obvious next question is which one comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this: a formula that closes a proof
Separate, on its own
The time when the כהן eats

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this
that the poor man's time is separate
and the priest's time is separate?
Yes, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שִׁעוּרָא דְּעָנִי לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 17 and overturns step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The poor man's time and the כהן's time are two different times.

steps.title: Which time comes later, the poor man's or the כהן's?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the two times are known to be different, the גמרא asks which one is later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which of the two is later?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the order of the two times. This sets up the reasoning in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the times are different does not tell us their order. The גמרא wants to know whether the poor man eats before or after the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Which of them?
Later

phrases.english: Which of them is later?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 18's conclusion that the two times differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the poor man's time is earlier or later than the כהן's time.

steps.title: The poor man must be later, or רבי חנינא would match רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that the poor man eats later. If he ate earlier, רבי חנינא would be saying the same thing as רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the poor man is later. Because if you say the poor man is earlier, then רבי חנינא would be the same as רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a logical argument: the poor man's time has to be later than the כהן's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר already holds the earliest time on the list. A time earlier than the כהן's would land on רבי אליעזר's time, so רבי חנינא would add nothing new. Since the ברייתא lists him as a separate opinion, his time must come after the כהן's.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it stands to reason
Earlier

phrases.english: It makes sense that the poor man is later,
because if you say the poor man is earlier,
then Rabbi Chanina is the same as Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: There's no room between רבי אליעזר's early time and the כהן's time, so an earlier poor man would just match רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The poor man's time is later, because an earlier time would make רבי חנינא the same as רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Conclusion: the poor man eats later than the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא firmly concludes that the poor man's time comes after the כהן's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it clear from here that the poor man is later? Yes, that is what we learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion and confirms that the poor man eats later than the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting it together: the poor man's time is different from the כהן's (step 18), and it comes after it (step 20). So רבי חנינא's time for the evening שמע is later than רבי יהושע's.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so: introduces a forced conclusion
A poor person, whose mealtime is used here to mark the time for שמע
That the poor man's time is later

steps.whatToRemember: The poor man's time and the כהן's time are different, and the poor man's time is later. Order of the times discussed: רבי אליעזר (earliest), then the כהן (רבי יהושע), then the poor man (רבי חנינא).

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּעָנִי מְאוּחָר.
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this that the poor man is later?
Yes, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּעָנִי מְאוּחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the reasoning of step 20 as the final answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The poor man's time is later than the כהן's time.

steps.title: רבי יהודה objects that the כהנים immerse while it is still day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's objection from the ברייתא: the כהנים immerse during the day, so their immersion cannot mark the start of the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהודה said to him: But don't the כהנים immerse while it is still day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes רבי יהודה's challenge to רבי מאיר, so it can now discuss it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר tied the start of evening קריאת שמע to the time the כהנים immerse. רבי יהודה attacks this: if the immersion happens during the day, it cannot be the start of nighttime שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day
Immerse in a מקוה
Priests, who immerse so they can eat תרומה

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Yehuda said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא כֹּהֲנִים מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם הֵם טוֹבְלִים!
phrases.english: But don't the priests immerse while it is still day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא כֹּהֲנִים מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם הֵם טוֹבְלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the analysis of רבי חנינא's time, the גמרא turns to the next line of the ברייתא, רבי יהודה's objection to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that evening שמע begins when the כהנים immerse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The immersion happens during the day, so it cannot mark the start of nighttime.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees that רבי יהודה's objection looks strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה is right. This shows that the objection seems correct and needs an answer for רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי יהודה speaking well to רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יהודה's objection seems correct. It is setting up the next move, where it explains how רבי מאיר would answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new attack. It makes the earlier objection stronger by admitting it looks right. Now רבי מאיר clearly has to be defended.

keyTerms.meaning: Well, correctly
He is saying

phrases.english: Is he speaking well to him,
Rabbi Yehuda to Rabbi Meir?
phrases.notes: The meaning is: his point seems right, so how would רבי מאיר answer it?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the force of the objection in step 22 and asks for רבי מאיר's response.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's objection seems correct, so רבי מאיר's view looks hard to hold.

steps.title: רבי מאיר means רבי יוסי's definition of twilight
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that he is not using רבי יהודה's definition of בין השמשות. He is using רבי יוסי's definition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר is saying this to him: Do you think I am talking about your בין השמשות? I am talking about רבי יוסי's בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי מאיר's answer: the two of them define twilight differently, so the objection does not apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's objection depends on his own long בין השמשות. By that definition, the immersion falls while it is still day. רבי מאיר holds like רבי יוסי, so the immersion falls at a different time.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the period between day and night
Do you think?
Yours

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not denying that the immersion comes before nightfall. He is saying the immersion he means comes at the end of the day, at רבי יוסי's split-second בין השמשות, right at צאת הכוכבים. It is not during רבי יהודה's long twilight, when it is still day.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir is saying this to him:
Do you think that I
am talking about your twilight?

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא אַבֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי קָא אָמֵינָא,
phrases.english: I am talking about Rabbi Yosei's twilight,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection that steps 22 and 23 raised and strengthened.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the terms: the two sages use different definitions of בין השמשות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר was using רבי יהודה's long twilight, so the immersion happens during the day.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר uses רבי יוסי's very short twilight, so the immersion is right at nightfall.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: twilight is only a blink of an eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוסי's statement that בין השמשות is only a blink of an eye and is too short to measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי said: בין השמשות is like the blink of an eye. This one comes in and that one goes out, and it is impossible to pin it down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי to explain what his definition of twilight is, which finishes רבי מאיר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, day ends and night begins in an instant, with almost no in-between time. So when the כהנים immerse just before that moment, it is already the edge of night. That is a fine start for evening שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the blink of an eye
One comes in and the other goes out (night comes, day leaves)
It is impossible to pin it down or measure it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's objection fails against רבי מאיר because רבי מאיר holds like רבי יוסי. For רבי יוסי, בין השמשות is a split second, so the כהנים's immersion is right at nightfall.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a debate about the time for שמע can depend on a deeper debate: how long בין השמשות lasts.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei said:
Twilight is like the blink of an eye;
this one comes in, and that one goes out,
phrases.notes: Night is coming in and day is going out, all in a single moment.

phrases.english: and it is impossible to pin it down.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת כְּהֶרֶף עַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and content of the רבי יוסי definition that רבי מאיר relied on in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בין השמשות is an instant too short to measure: day ends and night begins at once.
